For anyone who wants to read for the funda: Based on evidence accumulated this century, scientists estimate that the Americas had a population of about 60 million people when the Europeans arrived there in 1492. Most of the Native Americans were engaged in settled agriculture. Europe and China each had around 60 million people at that time. Within a few decades, the population of the Americas had dropped to just around 5 million people, with over 90% of people perishing due to a combination of infectious diseases and warfare. This population collapse resulted in agriculture being abandoned on a massive scale, resulting in farmland turning wild again. The disruption was big enough that it reduced the amount of CO2 in earth’s atmosphere. Evidence in ice cores from Antarctica shows lower amounts of atmospheric carbon dioxide in samples that are dated to the late 16th century. This reduction in CO2 led to climate change, and scientists now think it may be a key contributor to the phenomenon called the Little Ice Age. The Little Ice Age was a centuries-long period of lower temperatures that affected the North Atlantic region with particular severity. The Little Ice Age eventually ended only when humanity entered its first Industrial Revolution. At its height, the Little Ice Age caused what historians call The General Crisis of the 17th Century in Europe, a period of inclement weather, crop failure, economic hardship, extreme intergroup violence, and high mortality. The General Crisis culminated in the Thirty Years War, a continental-scale war lasting several decades, ending in the year 1648 with the Peace of Westphalia that established the concept of modern nation-states. By the time the Peace of Westphalia was concluded, populations in many regions of Europe had fallen by 70% compared to a generation earlier. ‎
